reviews.review:
This one is a mixed bag. I love that there's a new singleplayer deckbuilding rpg. I love the SRW series and so seeing something inspired by it immediately had me on board. The art looks nice and there's a good level of polish for the animations, and nice little touches like there being a ton of voice lines between characters during combat.

The reason I'm not recommending it boils down to two things, gameplay and story. 

Gameplay has two big issues. First, you don't get a traditional "hand of cards" like you would in most card games. Instead, every round you draw a suit and a drone and choose to deploy one of them, with the option to redraw once per round, to get a different potential suit/drone. Both are units, though drones are more focused on support and being a "at least it's not as bad as that other crappy main mech!".

This means that there isn't really any strategy you can use, holding cards to set up big plays. You've got to adapt on a turn by turn basis to what you're given, and it's alwasy very random.

There's that second part though. Why do you have crappy mechs in your deck in the first place? Because you can't build your deck. Any card you add to your collection goes into the deck forever and it just grows and grows. The more you level up, the more diluted your deck becomes. And this is made even worse because there are different factions and each has its own archetype. One is based on armor, for example. No other faction has armor, generates armor, or has armor payoffs. So the armor payoff mechs you get get weaker and weaker the more non-armor cards you get. This is the same for the other factions aside from the starting one which just has generic "does a lot of damage" as their gimmick.

Still, the lane-based gameplay of the card game aspect of the game can be fun too, and the game is mostly a visual novel anyways with nice looking art and full voice acting. Which brings me to the story.

It's an obvious ripoff of Super Robot Wars, that's not really being hidden. But the other thing it's a ripoff of is Star Trek. Every mission even starts with a "log date" diary. That's fine though. I love SRW, I love Star Trek (the stuff from before the 2000s + Lower Decks at least). 

I do not love these characters. I seriously gave it my best, letting the dialogue autoplay, trying to get attached to them, see where things are going. But my god. They're so damn boring. Every single character falls on a spectrum of "super nice and calm" to "super nice and quirky". About 20% of the conversations feel like "the crew is doing adventure things" and 80% is "the crew is saying nice and supportive things to each other". About 5 hours into the game, one of the main characters nearly dies and gets put into a medically induced coma... and I just don't care. I don't believe for a second the game has the balls to kill them off (they don't) but more importantly, the cast has done a poor job of endearing itself, so when things are meant to be heavy and dramatic, it just doesn't land. 

I start trying to skip scenes. There is a skip button, but the only way to make it appear is to click through dialogue rapidly. And when you then click the skip button, it only skips to the end of that scene. And there are about 5-10 scenes per mission. So it's a whole lot of button mashing, and eventually, not worth the trouble.
reviews.developer_response: In reponse to the gameplay portion of your thoughtful review: we've since added deck editing. The Skip button has also been tweaked to make it clearer that mashing isn't ever required. Cheers!
